what_worked: Attempted a coherent investor-thesis arc with bull/bear framing on the final slides.
fix_next: Nearly every quantitative claim is fabricated—categories, row count, total revenue, correlations all contradict the actual dataset. Start over from the data.
verdict: Polished-looking AI-generated deck built on almost entirely fabricated numbers.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2: Claims 1,047 startups (actual 1,000), $8.2B total MRR (actual ~$15.6M 30-day revenue), '94% completeness' unsupported. Slide 3: Categories listed as SaaS/Fintech/HealthTech/CleanTech—none match actual categories (AI, Marketing, E-comm, Education, etc.); SaaS at 27% is wrong (actual 66 of 726 categorized ≈9%); Fintech and HealthTech do not exist in dataset. Slide 4: Business model breakdown (Subscription 38%, Marketplace 22%, etc.) appears entirely invented; no such field structure in dataset. Slide 5: Revenue bins use MRR framing but dataset tracks 30-day revenue; bar chart unverifiable. Slide 6: $18.4M average valuation, $6.2M median, 8.3x ARR, 11x SaaS multiple—all fabricated; stock 'AlphaTech Global' screenshot is irrelevant decoration. Slide 7: Geographic percentages (NA 47%, Europe 29%, APAC 18%) and avg MRR figures fabricated; dataset has 'country' not 'region' and 241 missing. Slide 8: Claims r=0.71 for age vs MRR; actual founded-year/revenue r=0.025—off by ~29x; r=0.34 for funding vs MRR also unsupported. Slide 9-10: Recommendations rest on fabricated statistics (11x ARR, 62% MRR concentration, APAC growth rates).

evidence.insight: No genuine insight derived from the actual dataset; every analytical claim (categories, correlations, multiples) is fabricated, so there is nothing decision-useful.
evidence.narrative: There is a recognizable arc (overview → categories → models → revenue → geography → correlations → recommendations → thesis), giving partial credit for structure, but the story is built on invented facts.
evidence.framing: Audience is stated (investors/founders) but scope, definitions, and limitations are poorly handled—claims '94% completeness' and '1,047 startups' contradict the dataset; no mention of actual missingness patterns.
evidence.accuracy: At least 14 material factual errors: wrong n (1,047 vs 1,000), wrong total revenue ($8.2B vs ~$15.6M), entirely wrong category taxonomy, fabricated correlation (r=0.71 vs actual 0.025), invented valuation multiples, invented geographic splits. Essentially no claim checks out.
evidence.visual: Consistent dark-blue Gamma template is legible; chart types are reasonable in principle. However, slide 6 uses an irrelevant stock-ticker screenshot ('AlphaTech Global'), slide 9 uses AI-generated boardroom art, and slide 8's scatter plot has ~15 points for 1,000 rows. Decorative over evidential.
evidence.ai_slop: Pervasive: entire category taxonomy (SaaS/Fintech/HealthTech/CleanTech) appears hallucinated by AI; stock imagery on slides 6 and 9; consulting buzzwords ('asymmetric upside', 'barbell strategy', 'capital deployment') without data backing; Gamma watermark confirms AI tool with minimal human verification.
